CLIMATE NOTE

NOTE
Deep, closed upper low pressure over eastern Lake Erie tracks eastward toward New England through the day with moist cyclonic flow maintained in its wake across Southeast MI. Morning stratus evolves into stratocumulus as daytime mixing commences, with mostly cloudy skies prevailing through the day. Scattered early morning showers will move out leaving dry conditions the rest of the day save for a spotty sprinkle or two. The cold core of the system has already departed and will allow for high temps to rebound slightly compared to yesterday, landing in the lower 50s. A tight corridor of isentropic downglide accompanies the arrival of anticyclonic flow this afternoon, leading to rapid drying and the eventual clearing of remaining clouds this evening. Favorable radiating conditions cause temperatures to quickly drop this evening, settling into the lower 30s and upper 20s overnight. A Pacific jet streak arriving into the PNW causes the next Canadian shortwave to amplify as it tracks from southern Manitoba into the Great Lakes on Sunday. This wave induces a period of warm air advection on breezy southwesterly wind Sunday morning. Temperatures rebound into the mid 50s while afternoon wind becomes gusty to around 30 mph. The attendant surface low passes northeast of Georgian Bay late Sunday, dragging a cold front across the area. The greater lift tied to upper height falls and PVA will focus over Lake Huron, but a slight chance (20%) of light showers will exist along and behind the front Sunday evening. Cold air advection behind the Sunday wave is short-lived and temperatures will stay on the mild side into the mid-week. A progressive upper air pattern persists through this period with a shortwave ridge cresting overhead Monday before the next trough arrives on Tuesday. Fropa tied to this wave also looks mostly dry as the bulk of forcing slides north of the local area. By the end of the week, more persistent troughing develops across the Great Lakes and eastern CONUS. This will favor temperatures falling on the cooler side of average. Northerly flow shows potential for lake effect rain and snow showers at times. && .MARINE... Low pressure now located across the eastern Great Lakes will wash out across New England today. This will allow wind speeds to decrease through the late morning and afternoon hours and will bring light winds well into the evening. This window for lighter winds will be short-lived as a second low pressure system pushes from the central Canadian Provinces into southern Ontario and Quebec tomorrow. This will initially support breezy southwest flow with gusts at or below 30 knots, taking into consideration the more stable conditions under the stream of warm air aloft. However, as this low departs, winds will veer to the northwest, ushering in another round of cold air. The boost in instability over the warmer lake waters will help mixing depths tap the stronger winds aloft. This brings increasing confidence for gust to gales tomorrow afternoon through Monday morning across northern Lake Huron. A Gale Watch remains in effect. For locations south, Small Craft Advisories will be likely for the Saginaw Bay and portions of the Lake Huron shoreline as gust potential around 25 knots will be possible, in addition to the elevated wave heights across the Outer Saginaw Bay and Thumb under the initial southwest flow. && .PREV DISCUSSION... Issued at 1150 PM EST Fri Nov 6 2026 AVIATION... Compact mesoscale low pressure system is currently digging southward through the southern Lake Huron basin. Good wraparound deformation forcing exists with the back edge now pushing into the Saginaw Bay region. The center of the low will remain vertically stacked as parent vorticity maximum wobbles and digs southward to the eastern Lake Erie basin by 12z Saturday. Loss of daytime heating and vertical mixing has resulted in lowering ceilings. Dry air advection and return of daytime mixing will result in VFR sky conditions Saturday afternoon. DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES... * High for ceiling 5000 ft or less through Saturday morning. && .DTX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES... MI...None. Lake Huron...Small Craft Advisory until 10 AM EST this morning for LHZ422. Gale Watch from Sunday afternoon through Monday morning for LHZ361- 362. Small Craft Advisory until 4 PM EST this afternoon for LHZ421- 441>443. Lake St Clair...Small Craft Advisory until 10 AM EST this morning for LCZ460. Michigan waters of Lake Erie...None. && $$ DISCUSSION...TF MARINE.......AM AVIATION.....CB You can obtain your latest National Weather Service forecasts online at www.weather.gov/detroit.

.DISCUSSION...

Deep, closed upper low pressure over eastern Lake Erie tracks 
eastward toward New England through the day with moist cyclonic flow 
maintained in its wake across Southeast MI. Morning stratus evolves 
into stratocumulus as daytime mixing commences, with mostly cloudy 
skies prevailing through the day. Scattered early morning showers 
will move out leaving dry conditions the rest of the day save for a 
spotty sprinkle or two. The cold core of the system has already 
departed and will allow for high temps to rebound slightly compared 
to yesterday, landing in the lower 50s. A tight corridor of 
isentropic downglide accompanies the arrival of anticyclonic flow 
this afternoon, leading to rapid drying and the eventual clearing of 
remaining clouds this evening. Favorable radiating conditions cause 
temperatures to quickly drop this evening, settling into the lower 
30s and upper 20s overnight.

A Pacific jet streak arriving into the PNW causes the next Canadian 
shortwave to amplify as it tracks from southern Manitoba into the 
Great Lakes on Sunday. This wave induces a period of warm air 
advection on breezy southwesterly wind Sunday morning. Temperatures 
rebound into the mid 50s while afternoon wind becomes gusty to 
around 30 mph. The attendant surface low passes northeast of 
Georgian Bay late Sunday, dragging a cold front across the area. The 
greater lift tied to upper height falls and PVA will focus over Lake 
Huron, but a slight chance (20%) of light showers will exist along 
and behind the front Sunday evening.

Cold air advection behind the Sunday wave is short-lived and 
temperatures will stay on the mild side into the mid-week. A 
progressive upper air pattern persists through this period with a 
shortwave ridge cresting overhead Monday before the next trough 
arrives on Tuesday. Fropa tied to this wave also looks mostly dry as 
the bulk of forcing slides north of the local area. By the end of 
the week, more persistent troughing develops across the Great Lakes 
and eastern CONUS. This will favor temperatures falling on the 
cooler side of average. Northerly flow shows potential for lake 
effect rain and snow showers at times.

.MARINE...

Low pressure now located across the eastern Great Lakes will wash 
out across New England today. This will allow wind speeds to 
decrease through the late morning and afternoon hours and will bring 
light winds well into the evening. This window for lighter winds 
will be short-lived as a second low pressure system pushes from the 
central Canadian Provinces into southern Ontario and Quebec 
tomorrow. This will initially support breezy southwest flow with 
gusts at or below 30 knots, taking into consideration the more 
stable conditions under the stream of warm air aloft. However, as 
this low departs, winds will veer to the northwest, ushering in 
another round of cold air. The boost in instability over the warmer

This brings increasing confidence for gust to gales tomorrow
